name: Hip-Hop
def: Music built from the break — looped funk and soul samples, programmed beats and rhythmic spoken rhyme over the groove.

traits.v: Looped breakbeats with rhyme locked to the groove.
Sample-based loop construction and drum programming.
Rhythmic, rhymed speech (MCing).
Block-party, turntable and DJ culture.

why: It is loop-based construction: funk and soul breaks are looped and chopped, with rhyme riding the groove rather than melody.

albums.t: It Takes a Nation of Millions to Hold Us Back

tempoNote: Era-dependent — boom bap sits here; trap-era production runs 130–170 in half-time.

name: Contemporary R&B
def: Soul updated with hip-hop production — programmed beats, sampled loops and melismatic singing over swung, sub-heavy grooves.

traits.v: Hip-hop drum programming and sampling.
Melismatic, gospel-rooted lead and stacked harmony.
Swung, sub-bass-heavy groove.

why: Gospel-rooted soul singing is set over hip-hop's programmed, sample-based beats rather than a live band.

name: Trip-Hop
def: Downtempo, cinematic fusion of hip-hop's sampled breaks, dub bass and space and moody jazz and soul textures — head-nod music for headphones.

traits.v: Slow, swung hip-hop breakbeats.
Dub bass and space, vinyl crackle, jazzy samples.
Nocturnal, cinematic, melancholic.
Listening / late-night.

why: Hip-hop's sampled breaks are slowed and wrapped in dub bass and noir jazz atmosphere for listening rather than rapping.

name: Alternative R&B
def: A moody, atmospheric strain of R&B — spacious, alternative production and confessional songwriting that blurs soul with indie, ambient and electronic texture.

traits.v: Spacious, reverb-heavy, atmospheric production.
Intimate, confessional, often falsetto-led.
Post-2010 online, genre-agnostic R&B.

why: It pulls contemporary R&B toward atmosphere and introspection, borrowing dream-pop space and trip-hop's nocturnal mood.

tracks.why: Its hazy, guitar-lit intimacy set the template for a decade of atmospheric R&B.

name: Chopped & Screwed
def: Houston's remix technique turned genre — records dragged down to a crawl, beats stopped and doubled back by hand, the whole mix smeared into a syrupy haze.

traits.v: Turntable and tape pitched down to roughly 60–70% speed.
Chopped stutters — beats doubled, skipped and rewound live.
Deepened, blurred vocals over smeared low end.
Houston mixtape culture and DJ Screw's Screwed Up Click.

why: It proves tempo and pitch alone can make a different music — the same record, slowed, becomes narcotic and unfamiliar.

tracks.why: The most famous screwtape of all — thirty-odd minutes that defined the Houston sound.

tempoNote: Whatever the source record was, at roughly 60–70% speed.

name: Miami Bass
def: South Florida's party rap — Roland TR-808 drums, long sustained kicks and sub-bass at dance tempos under call-and-response chants and explicit lyrics.

traits.v: Electro-derived 808 patterns pushed to roughly 125–140 BPM.
Long, boomy 808 kick and sub-bass built for car and club systems.
Chanted, call-and-response party hooks, often sexually explicit.
Miami clubs, car-audio culture and independent labels like Luke Records.

why: It turned electro's drum machine into a bass-first party format, and its records became the raw material for Rio's funk carioca.

albums.t: As Nasty As They Wanna Be

tracks.why: The 808 kick and chant template the scene was built on.

name: Phonk
def: Internet-born hip-hop rebuilt from 90s Memphis rap tapes — lo-fi cassette grit, slowed and chopped vocal samples and TR-808 cowbell, later sped up into drift phonk.

traits.v: Samples of 90s Memphis rap tapes, pitched down and chopped.
Lo-fi hiss, blown-out 808s and the 808 cowbell as lead.
Slow Memphis bounce; drift phonk pushes it to fast, distorted club tempo.
SoundCloud, then TikTok and car-edit videos; a large Russian and Eastern European producer base.

why: It revived Memphis tape culture as an online genre, and its drift strain became one of the most-streamed sounds of the 2020s.

albums.t: Mysterious Phonk: The Chronicles of SpaceGhostPurrp

tracks.why: Cowbell lead and distorted bass — drift phonk at its streaming peak.
